inst_cams_intro: RTSP (Real Time Streaming Protocol) is the network address your IP cameras use to send their live video over the local network. CowCatcher AI reads that stream and analyses it frame by frame.
inst_cams_reolink: Reolink — RTSP is switched off at the factory, so you have to enable it once. Open the Reolink app on your computer or phone, select the camera, tap the gear icon and go to Network → Advanced → Server Settings. Tick RTSP and save. Confirm with Yes when the camera asks if you are sure.
inst_cams_hikvision: Hikvision & Dahua — RTSP is already enabled by default. You do not have to change anything in the camera software.
inst_cams_others: Axis, Foscam, Ubiquiti UniFi — also allow RTSP streaming out of the box, on the standard port 554.
inst_cams_ip_title: Find the IP address of your camera
inst_cams_ip_text: You need the IP address of the camera to connect it. You will find it in the camera's mobile app, on the network page of your router, or in the software of the camera brand. An IP address almost always looks like 192.168.1.31 or 192.168.178.50.
inst_cams_substream_text: Nearly every IP camera sends out two video streams: a mainstream in high resolution (4K or 1080p) that costs a lot of computing power, and a substream in a lower resolution (640x480 or 720p). For the AI the substream is more than sharp enough to recognise cows, mounting behaviour and calving activity — and it saves up to 80% of the load on your processor. Always pick the substream.
inst_stream_1: Open the folder of the web version and start the application. Your browser opens the local user interface.
inst_stream_2: If your browser or firewall asks for network access, choose Allow.
inst_stream_4: Enter a clear Label, for example Heifers barn 1 or Calving pen west.
inst_stream_5: Paste the RTSP address of the camera in the Source field. Use the template for your brand below.
inst_stream_6: Click Test. If the connection succeeds you immediately see the live camera image.
inst_stream_7: Click Save, and repeat these steps for every camera you want to add.
inst_stream_urls_note: Replace admin, PASSWORD and IP-ADDRESS with the details of your own camera.
inst_stream_caption: Streams → Add: give the camera a label, paste the RTSP URL and press Test before you save.
inst_tele_intro: Telegram is the fastest and cheapest way to receive alerts on your phone, including the photo of the detection.
inst_tele_2: Give the channel a Label, for example My phone or Family group.
inst_tele_3: Fill in the Token of your bot. You get this from Telegram’s BotFather when you create your own notification bot.
inst_tele_4: Fill in your Chat ID: a unique ten-digit number (for example 1234567890) that tells the bot which account or group chat the photos must go to.
inst_tele_5: Click Test notification and check your phone. Did the test message arrive? Then click Save.
inst_tele_caption: Notifications → Add Telegram: enter the bot token and your chat ID, then press ‘Test notification’.
inst_tele_groups_text: You can add as many Telegram recipients or groups as you like. A practical split: one group Heat detection heifers for the farmer and the staff, and a second group Calving alerts for the whole family or the night shift.
inst_tele_webhook_text: Do you use Home Assistant on the farm? Then you can also enter a webhook URL. CowCatcher AI sends a JSON signal to your Home Assistant server on every detection, so you can switch on the barn lighting automatically or trigger a physical siren relay.
inst_det_intro: In the Detectors tab you create the actual AI jobs: here you link the cameras, the type of detection and the settings together.
inst_det_cc_1: Click Add and choose the preset Cow Catcher (heat detection / mounting).
inst_det_cc_2: Select the streams that are aimed at the cows or heifers in heat.
inst_det_cc_3: Select the Telegram channels that must receive a message when a mount is detected.
inst_det_cc_4: Set the Confidence (see the table below) and click Save.
inst_det_calv_1: Click Add and choose the preset Calving Catcher.
inst_det_calv_2: Select the camera(s) of the calving pen or the straw boxes, plus the Telegram channels for calving alerts.
inst_det_calv_3: With calving you do not want any delay, so set the alert interval to 1: every detection is sent through immediately.
inst_det_calv_4: Set Required detected frames to about 15. The AI checks roughly once per second, so 15 seconds of continuous signal (feet or water bag) sets off the alarm.
inst_det_caption: Detectors → Add: pick a preset, link the streams and Telegram channels, and set the confidence.
inst_det_conf_intro: The confidence decides how sure the AI has to be of its case before an alert is sent.
inst_det_conf_092: Very strict. Virtually zero false alerts, but a very short or very fast mount can occasionally be missed.
inst_det_conf_090: Recommended setting. The ideal balance between a very high hit rate and minimal false alerts.
inst_det_conf_088: Sensitive. Registers practically everything, but gives a false alert now and then — for example when two cows stand close together.
inst_det_conf_085: Not recommended: too many false alerts.
inst_det_advanced_text: Behind the Advanced switch you will find extra parameters such as the detection interval, timeouts and video export. Everything you save here is written automatically to the config.json file in your program folder — you never have to edit that file by hand.
inst_start_1: Open the Cowcatcher folder and start the AI detector — the engine, not the web interface.
inst_start_2: A dark terminal window opens. Do not close this window! This is the engine that processes all the camera images in the background.
inst_start_3: On the very first start the program downloads the latest AI model from the server. Depending on your internet speed this takes one to three minutes. It then converts the model automatically to the fastest format for your hardware.
inst_start_log_text: Once the AI is active you see a line scroll by for every processed frame, with the detection time in milliseconds. As long as those lines keep coming, you know the AI is watching your barn live.
inst_start_caption: The engine’s terminal window: every line shows how long one frame took to process.
inst_storage_text: Every time the AI sees a mount or calving activity, two things happen: an alert goes straight to Telegram, and the photo with the AI box drawn on it is saved locally in the detections/ folder in your program folder. That way you automatically build up a local archive of every heat and calving moment, without depending on a cloud subscription. Your footage stays 100% on your own computer.
